title: When data stops fitting on one machine

videos.script: Ponto Final's website wrote twenty-four million events last year. Every page a visitor opened, every search, every book put in a basket. {{events}} Ana asked a simple question of it. How many different visitors looked at each book? Her program was correct. On a machine with a gigabyte to spare, it died after twenty-six seconds. {{died}} Nothing was wrong with the code. The data had grown past the machine. {{wall}} This lesson builds your lab: Java, Spark, and a cluster of three workers on your own computer. {{lab}} Then it runs Ana's question three ways. Once in memory, which fails. Once split by visitor, which works in a fraction of the memory. And once on the cluster, which is not faster at all. {{three}} That last result is the honest start of this course. A cluster is not a speed button. It is what you reach for when one machine has run out of something, and the first skill is knowing which thing. {{course}}
